name: mscse-prior-nd-undergrad-4xxxx
description: An MSCSE student who uploads the Notre Dame undergraduate transcript from their own B.S. (the 4+1 issues one transcript per career). The DGS, 2026-09-11: up to two 40000-level courses MAY count toward the MSCSE — "subject to all other constraints, so they should be listed … for further decisions & review" — so each one is counted only provisionally, cites §3.2's allowance rather than the Ph.D.'s §4.2, draws on §3.5's six credits shared with the bachelor's degree, and stays in the DGS review request until the approval exists. A 40000-level course the sheet blocks outright counts nothing whatever the student answers, and a course below the 40000 level never reaches the allowance at all.

detailIncludes: 6 of the 6 credits below the 60000 level used
6 of the 6 credits shared with your bachelor’s degree used

CSE 40113: pending DGS review — would count toward regular courses (3 cr) once approved
needs advisor + DGS approval per the rules sheet
CSE 40437: not counted — the rules sheet says this course does not count toward the MSCSE
CSE 20110: not relevant to the core knowledge requirement
